title: The Tehran Conference
setting: The Soviet embassy compound in Tehran. Roosevelt is lodged inside the Soviet perimeter, at Stalin's invitation and to Churchill's irritation. The Big Three are in the same room for the first time in the war, with interpreters at their shoulders and the shape of the peace already on the table.
stakes: The date of the second front, the postwar borders of Poland, and which of the three walks out having set the terms.

roles_in_scene.churchill: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, arguing from the weakest hand of the three and knowing it
roles_in_scene.stalin: Host, and the man whose armies have carried the war for two years
roles_in_scene.roosevelt-fdr: President of the United States, playing mediator and courting Stalin deliberately

ground_truth: Stalin presses hard for a firm date for the cross-Channel invasion and will not be deflected
Churchill advocates further Mediterranean operations and is steadily outmanoeuvred
Roosevelt sides with Stalin on Overlord and lets Churchill see it
Overlord is committed for May 1944 and a commander is to be named
Poland's postwar borders are shifted west in principle - the Curzon line in the east, German territory in compensation
Stalin undertakes to enter the war against Japan once Germany is defeated
opening_line: Tehran, the Soviet embassy. Three men who need each other and trust each other very little sit down to divide the future.
sources: Foreign Relations of the United States: The Conferences at Cairo and Tehran, 1943
Churchill, The Second World War, vol. V: Closing the Ring
